claim: Multisite modification is a basic way of conferring functionality to proteins and a key component of post-translational modification networks.
source: Multisite modification is a basic way of conferring functionality to proteins and a key component of post-translational modification networks.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a foundational premise of the paper.

claim: Under different instances of symmetry of the modification network, the biochemistry of multisite modification can lead to the symmetry being broken.
source: We demonstrate that under different instances of symmetry of the modification network (invoked explicitly or implicitly and discussed in the literature), the biochemistry of multisite modification can lead to the symmetry being broken.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the paper demonstrated through computational and analytical methods.

claim: Symmetry breaking can confer new capabilities to protein networks, including concentration robustness of different combinations of species in conjunction with multiple steady states.
source: Overall, through our study we show how symmetry breaking (i) can confer new capabilities to protein networks, including concentration robustness of different combinations of species (in conjunction with multiple steady states)
evidence: This is stated as a key finding in the abstract and demonstrated throughout the results section.

claim: Symmetry breaking could have been the basis for ordering of multisite modification, which is widely observed in cells.
source: (ii) could have been the basis for ordering of multisite modification, which is widely observed in cells
evidence: This is presented as a speculative interpretation of the findings in the abstract.

claim: Symmetry breaking can significantly impact information processing in multisite modification and in cell signalling networks/pathways where multisite modification is present.
source: (iii) can significantly impact information processing in multisite modification and in cell signalling networks/pathways where multisite modification is present
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the abstract based on the study's findings.

claim: Reversible phosphorylation and post-translational modification of proteins constitutes a basic way of conferring functionality to proteins in cells.
source: Reversible phosphorylation, and post-translational modification (PTM) of proteins in general, constitutes a basic way of conferring functionality to proteins in cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Basic modification mechanisms are capable of acting as complex molecular information processors.
source: interest in multisite modification stems from the fact that the basic modification mechanisms are capable of acting as complex molecular information processors (Conradi and Shiu, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Multisite modification mechanisms can exhibit switching and threshold behaviour.
source: Various studies have highlighted the possibilities of these mechanisms exhibiting switching and threshold behaviour (Markevich et al., 2004)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Multisite modification mechanisms can exhibit bistability/multistability.
source: bistability/multistability (Thomson and Gunawardena, 2009; Conradi and Mincheva, 2014
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Multisite modification mechanisms can exhibit oscillations.
source: oscillations Suwanmajo and Krishnan, 2015; Rubinstein et al., 2016; Suwanmajo et al., 2020)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Multisite modification mechanisms can exhibit biphasic dose–response curves.
source: biphasic dose–response curves (Suwanmajo and Krishnan, 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The rich repertoire of behaviour in multisite modification emerges from the most basic considerations and aspects of enzymatic modification of substrates.
source: We emphasize that this rich repertoire of behaviour emerges from the most basic considerations and aspects of enzymatic modification of substrates, and that this behaviour is a feature and a consequence of the modification network (rather than a single modification).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the literature in the introduction.

claim: Symmetry breaking is a fundamental theme in developmental biology for generating patterns.
source: A fundamental theme in developmental biology is the breaking of symmetry to generate patterns.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Strong experimental evidence for Turing-like mechanisms at the core of developmental regulation has been demonstrated in multiple model systems.
source: Strong experimental evidence for such mechanisms present at the core of developmental regulation has been demonstrated in multiple model systems (Onimaru et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Symmetry has been invoked as a key ingredient in the development of the MWC model which has been used to explain allostery in biomolecular information processing.
source: Symmetry has also been invoked as a key ingredient in the development of the MWC model which has been used to explain allostery in biomolecular information processing (Changeux, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Chiral symmetry breaking has been experimentally observed in crystallization of nanoparticles.
source: Chiral symmetry breaking has been experimentally observed in crystallization of nanoparticles (Hananel et al., 2019)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Chiral symmetry breaking has been experimentally observed in fibril formation from racemic mixtures.
source: fibril formation from racemic mixtures (Kushida et al., 2017)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Chiral symmetry breaking has been experimentally observed in the Soai reaction.
source: and in the Soai reaction (Soai et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The establishment of chirality has been postulated to be important in understanding the origins of life.
source: The establishment of such chirality has been postulated to be important in understanding the origins of life (Blackmond, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Many of the basic modification networks accommodate different types of symmetries.
source: In this regard, we note that (i) many of the basic modification networks accommodate different types of symmetries, as we discuss below.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the introduction and demonstrated in the results.

claim: Certain symmetries resulting in equal concentrations of different partial phosphoforms of a given level have been assumed in multiple contexts, sometimes implicitly.
source: (ii) Certain symmetries, for example, resulting in equal concentrations of different partial phosphoforms of a given level (Case 2 symmetry, discussed below) are not only plausible in vivo, but have also been assumed in multiple contexts, sometimes implicitly.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about the literature in the introduction.

claim: Case 3 symmetry has been found to be particularly desirable in enabling oscillatory behaviour.
source: (iv) Other symmetries (Case 3 symmetry, discussed below) have been found to be particularly desirable in enabling oscillatory behaviour: in fact, a thorough parametric analysis of oscillatory behaviour in certain random double-site modification networks reveals clusters in parameter space centred around parameter sets representing networks with this symmetry (Jolley et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The ordering of multisite modification is a fundamental aspect of substrate modification and its regulation.
source: The ordering of multisite modification is a fundamental aspect of substrate modification and its regulation, and the deployment of modified substrates in various processes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The ordering of multisite modification has been the focus of different studies spanning canonical pathways, important cellular processes, basic principles, and engineering for synthetic biology.
source: It has been the focus of different studies (Kocieniewski et al., 2012; Lyons et al., 2013; Lössl et al., 2016; Valk et al., 2014) spanning canonical pathways, important cellular processes, basic principles, and engineering for synthetic biology.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In the ordered double-site modification network with common kinase and common phosphatase, the symmetric steady state loses stability via a supercritical pitchfork bifurcation as total substrate concentration is varied.
source: However as the total substrate concentration is varied, we find that this steady state loses stability via a supercritical pitchfork bifurcation (Strogatz, 2001).
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and analytically in the results section.

claim: In the ordered double-site modification network with common kinase and common phosphatase, a pair of asymmetric steady states emerge which are stable after the bifurcation.
source: A pair of asymmetric steady states emerge which are stable.
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and analytically in the results section.

claim: The nonlinearity responsible for symmetry breaking in the ordered double-site modification system arises purely from sequestration effects with no explicit feedback present.
source: It is worth emphasizing here that (i) the nonlinearity responsible for the symmetry breaking arises purely from sequestration effects with no explicit feedback present
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the analytical results.

claim: A single-site modification system is incapable of intrinsically exhibiting symmetry breaking behaviour.
source: and (ii) an analogous case of single-site modification is incapable of intrinsically exhibiting such behaviour.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the results section.

claim: The symmetry breaking observed in the ordered modification mechanism is also seen in the random modification with common kinase and phosphatase.
source: The symmetry breaking observed in this ordered mechanism is seen in the random modification with common kinase and phosphatase (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In the random modification network with common kinase and phosphatase, beyond the bifurcation point, the concentrations of both partial phosphoforms remain fixed at their values at the bifurcation point.
source: In this instance, beyond the bifurcation point, the concentrations of both partial phosphoforms remain fixed at their values at the bifurcation point. This is established analytically (see Appendix 1, Source code 1 [Section 3.1], and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and established analytically in the results section.

claim: Random mechanisms with different kinases and phosphatases can exhibit Case 1 symmetry breaking.
source: Random mechanisms with different kinases and phosphatases can also exhibit the same type of symmetry (this places constraints on total concentrations of 'corresponding' enzymes, in addition to the kinetic constraints already discussed). As seen in Figure 2C, this system also exhibits a similar symmetry-breaking behaviour as encountered above
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: In the random modification network with different kinases and phosphatases, the concentration of partial phosphoforms is fixed beyond the bifurcation.
source: and here again the concentration of partial phosphoforms is fixed beyond the bifurcation.
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and established analytically in the results section.

claim: Each leg of the random modification network with different kinases and phosphatases corresponds to an ordered modification mechanism with different kinases and phosphatases, which is incapable of symmetry breaking.
source: Each leg of the modification corresponds to an ordered modification mechanism with different kinases and phosphatases, which is incapable of symmetry breaking (as shown in Source code 1 [Section 2.2] and Supplementary file 1) and multistability in general.
evidence: This is established analytically in the results section.

claim: The observed symmetry breaking in the random modification network with different kinases and phosphatases is an emergent behaviour of the entire network with both modification legs.
source: Thus the observed symmetry breaking is an emergent behaviour of the entire network with both modification legs.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the analytical results.

claim: The case of common kinase and common phosphatase will not lead to the breaking of Case 2 symmetry.
source: Examining all the cases of random networks together (Figure 1A–C) reveals the following insights: (i) the case of common kinase and common phosphatase will not lead to the breaking of this symmetry.
evidence: This is demonstrated analytically in the results section.

claim: The case of different kinase and common phosphatase will not lead to the breaking of Case 2 symmetry.
source: (ii) The case of different kinase and common phosphatase will also not lead to the breaking of this symmetry.
evidence: This is demonstrated analytically in the results section.

claim: For the common kinase and common phosphatase case, the partial phosphoforms necessarily must have equal concentrations at any steady state irrespective of parameters.
source: In both cases, this can be shown directly analytically by demonstrating that for any steady states (irrespective of parameters) the partial phosphoforms necessarily must have equal concentrations (see Source code 1 [Sections 3.1 and 3.2] and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is established analytically in the results section.

claim: An identical conclusion about equal partial phosphoform concentrations can be drawn for the common kinase common phosphatase case, irrespective of the number of modification sites.
source: Incidentally, an identical conclusion can be drawn for the common kinase common phosphatase case, irrespective of the number of modification sites.
evidence: This is stated as an extension of the analytical results.

claim: The case of different kinase and different phosphatase can exhibit the breaking of Case 2 symmetry.
source: (iii) On the other hand, the case of different kinase and different phosphatase can indeed exhibit the breaking of this symmetry (Figure 2D) via a supercritical pitchfork bifurcation
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In the case of different kinase and different phosphatase with Case 2 symmetry breaking, the asymmetric steady states are characterized by fixed values of concentrations of unmodified and fully modified phosphoforms.
source: here the asymmetric steady states are characterized by fixed values of concentrations of unmodified and fully modified phosphoforms. This is established analytically (see Source code 1 [Section 3.3] and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and established analytically in the results section.

claim: In the separate kinase common phosphatase network with processive dephosphorylation, if the kinase is common to different phosphorylation steps, the Case 2 symmetry does not break.
source: Here we find that if the kinase is common to different phosphorylation steps, the symmetry does not break
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and analytically in the results section.

claim: In the separate kinase common phosphatase network with processive dephosphorylation, when the kinases are different, Case 2 symmetry breaking does happen.
source: however, surprisingly when the kinases are different, symmetry breaking does indeed happen, as shown in Figure 2E (again reinforcing the flexibility provided by having different enzymes in enabling such behaviour).
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Having processive dephosphorylation while reducing the nonlinearity in the network actually enables Case 2 symmetry breaking which was otherwise precluded in the different kinase common phosphatase random mechanism.
source: A direct comparison with the different kinase common phosphatase random mechanism above reveals a new dimension: having processive dephosphorylation while reducing the nonlinearity in the network actually enables this behaviour which was otherwise precluded.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the computational results.

claim: Different conditions in the cell or stimuli could effect a transition from distributive to processive mechanisms.
source: We also note that different conditions in the cell (or stimuli) could effect a transition from distributive to processive mechanisms, as demonstrated (Aoki et al., 2013; Aoki et al., 2011; Kocieniewski et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In Case 3 symmetry breaking, both symmetries necessarily break together in general.
source: The noteworthy point here is that both symmetries necessarily break together in general.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the results section and established analytically.

claim: In Case 3 symmetry breaking in the common kinase common phosphatase case, a subcritical pitchfork bifurcation is possible.
source: One is the possibility of a subcritical pitchfork bifurcation (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In the subcritical pitchfork bifurcation scenario for Case 3 symmetry, the branches of asymmetric states are unstable at the point of inception, but following a saddle node bifurcation, they become stable.
source: In such a case, the branches of asymmetric states are unstable at the point of inception, but following a saddle node bifurcation, they become stable.
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally in the results section.

claim: In Case 3 symmetry breaking in the common kinase common phosphatase case, the sum of partial phosphoform concentrations remains fixed on the asymmetric branches.
source: Irrespective of the nature of the pitchfork bifurcation (supercritical or subcritical), we find that the sum of partial phosphoform concentrations remains fixed on the asymmetric branches, and this is established analytically (see Appendix 1, Source code 1 [Section 3.1], and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and established analytically in the results section.

claim: In Case 3 symmetry breaking in the common kinase common phosphatase case, oscillations can emerge via a Hopf bifurcation, and this precedes the subcritical pitchfork bifurcation.
source: Another behaviour which is observed in a different parameter regime is the emergence of oscillations, via a Hopf bifurcation, and this precedes the subcritical pitchfork bifurcation (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The oscillations in Case 3 symmetry breaking do not preserve the symmetry of the original system.
source: The oscillations do not preserve the symmetry of the original system.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the computational results.

claim: In Case 3 symmetry breaking in the separate kinase separate phosphatase case, symmetry breaking occurs via supercritical pitchfork bifurcations but not subcritical pitchfork bifurcations.
source: Here (Figure 3B), we again find symmetry breaking via supercritical pitchfork bifurcations (but not subcritical pitchfork bifurcations)
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In Case 3 symmetry breaking in the separate kinase separate phosphatase case, the symmetry-broken states necessarily have both symmetries broken.
source: and the symmetry-broken states (which necessarily have both symmetries broken: see Source code 1 [Section 3.3] and Supplementary file 1)
evidence: This is established analytically in the results section.

claim: In Case 3 symmetry breaking in the separate kinase separate phosphatase case, either the sum of partial phosphoform concentrations or the sum of concentrations of A00 and A11 is approximately constant depending on parameters.
source: Here an exact invariant of the form examined previously does not hold: instead we find that (depending on parameters) either the sum of partial phosphoform concentrations or the sum of concentrations of A00 and A11 is approximately constant (see Figure 3, Appendix 2—figure 4, Source code 1 [Section 3.3], and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and established analytically in the results section.

claim: The possibility of oscillations emerging is seen in Case 3 symmetry breaking in the separate kinase separate phosphatase case.
source: The possibility of oscillations (stable over a broad range of parameters) emerging is also seen here (Figure 3B)
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Enzyme sequestration and competition provides the key nonlinearity for generating symmetry breaking obviating the need for explicit feedback.
source: Enzyme sequestration (and competition) provides the key nonlinearity for generating symmetry breaking obviating the need for explicit feedback.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results in the discussion.

claim: Eliminating enzyme sequestration eliminates the possibility of symmetry breaking.
source: Eliminating enzyme sequestration eliminates the possibility of symmetry breaking.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the discussion.

claim: The symmetry breaking found does not require any explicit assumption on the kinetic regime of enzymatic action.
source: However, the symmetry breaking we have found does not require any explicit assumption on the kinetic regime of enzymatic action (as seen from the sufficient conditions we have obtained) and so zeroth-order ultrasensitivity is neither necessary nor sufficient for this.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the analytical results in the discussion.

claim: Multisite modification systems encountered in vivo often exhibit different degrees of ordering ranging from complete ordering of the sequence of modifications, to partial ordering, to a complete absence of ordering.
source: Multisite modification systems encountered in vivo often exhibit different degrees of ordering ranging from complete ordering of the sequence of modifications, to partial ordering, to a complete absence of ordering (symmetric scenario).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion.

claim: The basic biochemistry of multisite modification by itself provides the basis for creating an ordering by breaking symmetry.
source: Our results indicate that the basic biochemistry of multisite modification by itself provides the basis for creating an ordering by breaking symmetry.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results in the discussion.

claim: Symmetry breaking demonstrates that a key driving factor for ordering could be at the modification network level rather than at the molecular level.
source: This demonstrates that a key driving factor could be at the modification network level rather than at the molecular level.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results in the discussion.

claim: Symmetry breaking allows for a mechanism whereby changing one easy to manipulate parameter (expression level of substrate) establishes a significant biasing of one pathway over the other.
source: Symmetry breaking allows for a distinct mechanism whereby changing one easy to manipulate parameter (expression level of substrate), a significant biasing of one pathway over the other is established.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results in the discussion.

claim: Multisite modification contains an in-built mechanism of creating robustness for clusters of species, either individually or collectively.
source: From the above points, we see that multisite modification contains an in-built mechanism of creating robustness for clusters of species, either individually or collectively, something which represents an appealing characteristic for natural and engineered modification networks.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results in the discussion.

claim: The mechanism of absolute concentration robustness seen in multisite modification shares a feature with ACR observed in autocatalytic networks, arising from a transcritical bifurcation, as being intimately tied to a nonlinear dynamic transition arising from the biochemistry.
source: The mechanism seen here shares a feature of ACR observed in autocatalytic networks, arising from a transcritical bifurcation (Shinar and Feinberg, 2011; Krishnan and Floros, 2019) as being intimately tied to a nonlinear dynamic transition arising from the biochemistry.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results in the discussion, supported by citations.

claim: Absolute concentration robustness in the ordered DSP network necessarily requires multiple steady states, with two branches of steady states exhibiting ACR.
source: (ii) ACR necessarily requires multiple steady states, with two branches of steady states exhibiting ACR.There is another steady-state branch which does not exhibit ACR, but intersects one of the branches in what was computationally observed to be a transcritical bifurcation.
evidence: This is established analytically in the discussion.

claim: There is a constraint on parameters to enable absolute concentration robustness in the ordered DSP network, which is weaker than the symmetry condition.
source: (iii) There is a constraint on parameters to enable this, which is weaker than the symmetry condition.
evidence: This is established analytically in the discussion.

claim: In the case of symmetry in the ordered DSP network, the two ACR branches are symmetric and intersect with the other branch in a pitchfork bifurcation.
source: (iv) In the case of symmetry, the two ACR branches are symmetric and intersect with the other branch in a pitchfork bifurcation.
evidence: This is established analytically in the discussion.

claim: Symmetry breaking in multisite modification allows for both regulation of downstream pathways as well as insulation of some downstream pathways from the effect of total upstream substrate and other upstream perturbations via ACR for specific substrates.
source: Here the symmetry breaking allows for both regulation of downstream pathways as well as insulation of some downstream pathways from the effect of total upstream substrate and other upstream perturbations (via ACR for specific substrates in the modification network).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results in the discussion.

claim: Shared ACR where the sum of two species concentrations is fixed represents a case where robustness is applied to a combination of pathways if the two species regulate different pathways.
source: This represents a case where robustness is applied to a combination of pathways if the two species regulate different pathways.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results in the discussion.

claim: The sequestration of a substrate species in a downstream complex can either facilitate or make difficult the possibility of symmetry breaking.
source: (iii) The effect of sequestration of a substrate species can be to either facilitate or make difficult the possibility of symmetry breaking.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results in the discussion.

claim: A detailed computational study reveals regions of parameter space which facilitate the presence of oscillations in random networks with common kinase and common phosphatase, and the prominent regions are clustered around a symmetric network (Case 3).
source: A detailed computational study (Jolley et al., 2012) reveals regions of parameter space which facilitate the presence of oscillations, and the prominent regions are clustered around a symmetric network (the Case 3 network that we have studied).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: By varying total enzyme amounts, it is possible to obtain multistability, oscillations or a combination of such behaviour in Case 3 symmetry breaking.
source: In the latter case, we demonstrate that by varying total enzyme amounts (easily tuneable dials) it is possible to obtain, multistability, oscillations or a combination of such behaviour (see Appendix 2—figure 7).
evidence: This is demonstrated computationally and shown in Appendix 2—figure 7.

claim: Symmetry breaking may occur, limiting/preventing a range of oscillations in certain cases.
source: It indicates how in certain cases symmetry breaking may occur, limiting/preventing a range of oscillations.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results in the discussion.

claim: Oscillations do not have to be present for an indefinitely large range in Case 3 symmetry breaking.
source: In particular, it indicates that oscillations do not have to be present for an indefinitely large range (suggested in the computations of Jolley et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results in the discussion, contrasting with prior work.
